draftA:
Lesson Plan: Unit Rates with Fractions (Grade 7, 45 minutes)
Standard: 7.RP.A.1. Compute unit rates from ratios of fractions.
Class: 28 students. 4 need reading support, so all problems use short sentences.

1. Warm-up (5 min): Divide fractions. 1/2 ÷ 1/4 = 2. 3/4 ÷ 1/2 = 3/2.

2. Worked Example (10 min): Ana walks 1/2 mile. It takes 1/4 hour. Find miles per hour. (1/2) ÷ (1/4) = 2. Unit rate: 2 miles per hour.

3. Guided Practice (10 min): In pairs. Ben runs 3/4 mile. It takes 1/4 hour. Miles per hour? Answer: 3.

4. Independent Practice (12 min): A tap fills 2/5 of a tank. It takes 1/5 hour. Tanks per hour? Answer: 2.

5. Exit Quiz (8 min): Five questions below.

Quiz
1. A snail moves 1/3 foot. It takes 1/6 minute. Feet per minute?
2. Sam paints 3/4 of a wall. It takes 1/2 hour. Walls per hour?
3. A recipe uses 2/3 cup of sugar. It makes 1/3 of a batch. Cups per batch?
4. Mia paints 5/6 square meter. It takes 1/3 hour. Square meters per hour?
5. A car uses 3/5 gallon. It goes 9 miles. Miles per gallon?

Answer Key
1. (1/3) ÷ (1/6) = 2 feet per minute
2. (3/4) ÷ (1/2) = 1 1/2 walls per hour
3. (2/3) ÷ (1/3) = 2 cups per batch
4. (5/6) ÷ (1/3) = 2 1/2 square meters per hour
5. 9 ÷ (3/5) = 15 miles per gallon
draftB:
45-minute Grade 7 lesson. Standard 7.RP.A.1: compute unit rates from ratios of fractions, including lengths, areas, and like or different units. Class of 28. Four need reading support, so use short sentences. Flow: warm-up, worked example, guided practice, independent practice, exit quiz.

Warm-up, 5 min. Unit rate means per 1 unit. 6 miles in 2 hours is 3 miles per hour.

Worked example, 10 min. Path: 3/4 mile in 1/2 hour. Divide 3/4 by 1/2. Reciprocal: 3/4 times 2/1 = 3/2 miles per hour.

Guided practice, 10 min. Paint: 1/2 square foot in 1/4 hour. 1/2 divided by 1/4 = 2 square feet per hour. Check steps as a class.

Independent practice, 10 min. A: 1/3 mile in 1/6 hour. Miles per hour? B: 2/5 square foot in 1/5 hour. Square feet per hour? Help the four readers. Answers: 2 and 2.

Exit quiz, 10 min.

Quiz
1. A unit rate is per how many units?
2. 2/3 divided by 1/6 = ?
3. Rope: 4/5 m weighs 2/5 kg. Kg per meter?
4. Field: 1/2 acre in 1/4 hour. Acres per hour?
5. 3/8 divided by 3/4 = ?

Answer key
1. 1
2. 4
3. 1/2 kg per meter
4. 2 acres per hour
5. 1/2

reviewOfA.strengths: The lesson follows the required five-part structure, totals 45 minutes, and every unit-rate calculation in the plan and answer key is correct.

findings.title: Quiz item repeats guided practice
findings.detail: Quiz 4 uses the same numbers as guided practice: 1/2 divided by 1/4 = 2. Students can recall the answer instead of computing it. Independent practice answers are also both 2. Varying the numbers would show real mastery.
findings.quote: 4. Field: 1/2 acre in 1/4 hour. Acres per hour?

findings.title: Field question lacks an action
findings.detail: The item has no verb, so the scenario is unclear (mowed? planted?). The four students needing reading support may struggle with it. A short sentence such as 'A farmer mows 1/2 acre in 1/4 hour' would be clearer.

findings.title: Two quiz items lack rate context
findings.detail: Items 2 and 5 are bare fraction divisions with no quantities or units. They test a skill but not unit rates, which the standard requires. Adding short contexts would align them with 7.RP.A.1.

reviewOfB.strengths: Every calculation is correct and the timings sum exactly to 45 minutes, following the department's five-part lesson structure.

merge.document:
Lesson Plan: Unit Rates with Fractions (Grade 7, 45 minutes)
Standard: 7.RP.A.1. Compute unit rates from ratios of fractions, including lengths, areas and like or different units.
Class: 28 students. 4 need reading support, so all problems use short sentences.
Flow: warm-up, worked example, guided practice, independent practice, exit quiz.

1. Warm-up (5 min): A unit rate means per 1 unit. 6 miles in 2 hours is 3 miles per hour. Divide fractions: 1/2 ÷ 1/4 = 1/2 × 4/1 = 2.

2. Worked Example (10 min): Ana walks 3/4 mile. It takes 1/2 hour. Find miles per hour. 3/4 ÷ 1/2 = 3/4 × 2/1 = 3/2. Unit rate: 1 1/2 miles per hour.

3. Guided Practice (10 min): In pairs. Ben paints 1/2 square foot. It takes 1/4 hour. Square feet per hour? 1/2 × 4/1 = 2. Check steps as a class.

4. Independent Practice (10 min): A. Kim runs 3/4 mile. It takes 1/4 hour. Miles per hour? B. A tap fills 2/5 of a tank. It takes 1/5 hour. Tanks per hour? Help the four readers. Answers: 3 and 2.

5. Exit Quiz (10 min): Five questions below.

Quiz
1. A snail moves 1/3 foot. It takes 1/6 minute. Feet per minute?
2. A rope is 4/5 meter long. It weighs 2/5 kg. Kg per meter?
3. A farmer mows 2/3 acre. It takes 1/6 hour. Acres per hour?
4. Mia paints 5/6 square meter. It takes 1/3 hour. Square meters per hour?
5. A recipe uses 3/8 cup of sugar. It makes 3/4 of a batch. Cups per batch?

Answer Key
1. 1/3 ÷ 1/6 = 1/3 × 6/1 = 2 feet per minute
2. 2/5 ÷ 4/5 = 2/5 × 5/4 = 1/2 kg per meter
3. 2/3 ÷ 1/6 = 2/3 × 6/1 = 4 acres per hour
4. 5/6 ÷ 1/3 = 5/6 × 3/1 = 2 1/2 square meters per hour
5. 3/8 ÷ 3/4 = 3/8 × 4/3 = 1/2 cup per batch
merge.keptFromA: From draft A I kept the numbered five-part plan layout, the short two-sentence word problems for the reading-support students, and the snail, tap and Mia area quiz items with worked answers.
merge.keptFromB: From draft B I kept the unit-rate definition warm-up, the reciprocal method, the 10-minute timings, the rope item with different units, and its fraction divisions recast as context problems.

resolutions.finding: D-B1 Quiz item repeats guided practice
resolutions.note: The field item now uses 2/3 acre in 1/6 hour (answer 4), which appears nowhere in the lesson. Independent practice answers are now 3 and 2, and no quiz item reuses lesson numbers.

resolutions.finding: D-B2 Field question lacks an action
resolutions.note: Rewritten as short sentences with a verb: 'A farmer mows 2/3 acre. It takes 1/6 hour. Acres per hour?'

resolutions.finding: D-B3 Two quiz items lack rate context
resolutions.note: Bare division 2/3 ÷ 1/6 became the farmer mowing rate (4 acres per hour). Bare division 3/8 ÷ 3/4 became the recipe rate (1/2 cup per batch). All five items are now unit-rate problems with units.

finalReview.strengths: Every unit-rate calculation checks out, the five-part flow matches the department guide, and the timed sections add to 45 minutes.
